title: FOMC Meeting Minutes
timezone: Publication time shown in UTC; dashboard clock uses SGT
dissent: Lisa D. Cook and Beth M. Hammack preferred a 25 bp increase at the October meeting.
executive_summary: The Committee held rates unchanged to gather more information, but the minutes show broad support for additional tightening under the baseline outlook. Inflation remained elevated, activity was expanding at a solid pace and labour conditions were broadly stable. This is hawkish forward guidance, not an October rate hike.

key_findings.label: Policy decision
key_findings.detail: 10 members supported holding; two preferred a 25 bp increase.

key_findings.label: Forward guidance
key_findings.detail: Almost all participants judged further increases would likely be appropriate under their baseline outlook.

key_findings.label: December risk
key_findings.value: Larger than 25 bp not ruled out
key_findings.detail: A couple of participants said a move greater than 25 bp could be considered if incoming inflation data were unfavourable.

key_findings.label: Inflation
key_findings.detail: Staff estimated September total PCE at 3.6% and core PCE at 3.1%; both above the 2% goal.

key_findings.label: Growth and labour
key_findings.detail: Economic activity was expanding at a solid pace; unemployment edged up to 4.2%, while payroll gains averaged about 50,000 over three months.

key_findings.label: Market pricing
key_findings.detail: Futures implied a high probability of a 25 bp hike by year-end and two more by summer 2027; the path was little changed over the intermeeting period.

interpretation.strength: High confidence in hawkish direction; medium confidence in the size and timing of the next move.
interpretation.why: The key surprise is not an immediate policy change. It is the breadth of support for additional tightening and the explicit willingness by a couple of participants to consider a larger move if inflation disappoints.
interpretation.market_caveat: Because markets already assigned a high probability to further tightening, the minutes alone may not generate a sustained USD rally. Follow-through depends on new inflation, labour-market data, front-end yields and whether other central banks turn relatively less hawkish.

fx_implications.reason: Potential pressure if US front-end yields outperform euro-area yields; reassess against ECB guidance and euro-area growth/fiscal risks.
Potential pressure if Fed tightening expectations rise relative to BoE expectations; UK inflation and wage data remain decisive.
Higher US yields can support the pair, but BoJ tightening and intervention risk can materially offset the differential.
Relative Fed/RBA repricing matters; AUD is also sensitive to China, commodities and global risk appetite.
Relative Fed/RBNZ rate expectations matter; domestic growth and risk sentiment can dominate.
Fed-BoC rate differentials matter, but oil prices and Canadian data can overwhelm the USD impulse.
Rate differentials may favour USD, while safe-haven demand and SNB expectations can alter the response.

horizons.watch: US 2-year Treasury yield, Fed funds futures and the first FX reaction. Avoid assuming the first move will persist.
US CPI/PCE, employment releases, Fed speakers and whether market pricing shifts beyond what was already discounted.
December FOMC decision, updated Fed guidance and policy expectations from the ECB, BoE, BoJ, SNB, BoC, RBA and RBNZ.

trader_plan: Treat the minutes as a hawkish hold, not as a fresh rate hike.
Prioritise relative-value comparisons: Fed expectations versus each counterpart central bank.
Confirm the thesis with US 2-year yields and post-data market pricing before favouring USD trades.
For USD/JPY, explicitly account for BoJ repricing and Japanese intervention risk.
Wait for the existing D1/H4 structure, key levels and risk/reward rules; the minutes do not provide an entry price.
invalidation: US inflation and wage data soften enough to reduce expected Fed tightening.
US front-end yields fall and Fed futures materially remove expected hikes.
Counterpart central banks reprice more hawkishly than the Fed.
Risk-off or safe-haven flows dominate the rate-differential channel.

methodology.policy_momentum: Qualitative editorial classification; not a calibrated numerical score.
methodology.currency_score: Not added to the existing structural or economic event score. No double counting.
methodology.pair_bias: Conditional macro implications only; not live signals or guaranteed forecasts.
methodology.refresh: Eight-bank policy snapshots are manually curated from official central-bank sources and dated. This version does not yet auto-ingest speeches/minutes or regenerate AI summaries; refresh after each new decision or material communication.

coverage_note: Eight-bank snapshot based on the latest available official policy decision or official policy communication identified as of 19 November 2026. Rates are not directly comparable across operating frameworks; ECB uses the deposit facility rate and the Fed uses the target range.

central_banks.name: Federal Reserve
central_banks.summary: October minutes show broad support for further tightening under the baseline outlook; two members preferred a 25 bp hike at that meeting.

central_banks.name: European Central Bank
central_banks.summary: Energy shock raises inflation risks but also weighs on growth; underlying inflation broadly stable and no pre-commitment to a rate path.

central_banks.name: Bank of England
central_banks.summary: MPC voted 8–1 to raise Bank Rate; energy-driven inflation pressures and UK CPI at 3.5% in September were key concerns.

central_banks.name: Bank of Japan
central_banks.summary: Held at around 1.25%; one board member proposed 1.50%. October outlook says the Bank will continue raising rates as activity, prices and financial conditions evolve.

central_banks.name: Swiss National Bank
central_banks.summary: Rate unchanged; inflation remains within the price-stability range and the SNB remains willing to intervene in FX if needed.

central_banks.name: Reserve Bank of Australia
central_banks.summary: Raised by 25 bp with a 6–3 vote; broad-based inflation and domestic capacity pressures drove the decision.

central_banks.name: Reserve Bank of New Zealand
central_banks.summary: Raised OCR to 2.75%; inflation rose to 4.1% in Q2, while the Bank expected underlying inflation to return toward target over time.

central_banks.name: Bank of Canada
central_banks.summary: Raised the overnight rate by 25 bp to 2.50%; global resilience and persistent energy-price pressures informed the decision.
central_banks.source_name: Bank of Canada policy decision, 28 Oct 2026

relative_policy_method: Ordinal editorial comparison of the latest policy tone, not a numerical currency-strength score. A more hawkish tone can support a currency only if it is more hawkish than markets expected and than the counterpart central bank. The 28-pair watchlist is a research prompt, not a forecast or trade signal.
